# autodiff.AutodiffPropagation { #clerq.autodiff.AutodiffPropagation }

```python
autodiff.AutodiffPropagation(
    setup,
    *,
    step='ab',
    strategy='s3',
    checkpoints=None,
    rtol=1e-08,
    atol=1e-10,
    max_steps=100000,
    n_steps=None,
    solver=None,
)
```

A differentiable version of a :class:`~clerq.PropagationSolver` problem.

Build it with :meth:`clerq.PropagationSolver.to_autodiff`. It reproduces
``PropagationSolver.solve`` as a pure function of a *parameter pytree*, so the
propagated field and any loss of it can be differentiated with respect to the
parameters, with reverse- or forward-mode autodiff, and composed with
``jax.jit``, ``jax.vmap`` and optimisers.

Parameters are a ``dict``; every key is optional and defaults to the value
in the problem (see :meth:`default_params`):

``pulse_args``
    list, one dict per field, of the arguments of its analytic input pulse
    (``ampl``, ``centre``, ``fwhm``/``width``, ``n_pi``, ``on``, ``off``).
    The ``on``/``off`` edge times of a ``square`` pulse can be set but not
    differentiated (the field is discontinuous there, so its derivative is a
    delta function that autodiff would return as 0); ``value_and_grad``
    raises if asked, and holds them fixed by default. To differentiate
    the edge times use a ramp pulse (``ramp_on``, ``ramp_off``,
    ``ramp_onoff``, ``ramp_offon``), whose edges are smooth. Calling
    ``jax.grad`` yourself through :meth:`propagate` with those traced
    gives exactly that silent 0, so keep them out of the differentiated
    parameters.
``rabi_freq``
    array ``(n_fields,)``, cyclic ``rabi_freq`` multiplying each pulse.
``interaction_strengths``
    array ``(n_fields,)``, as the ``interaction_strengths`` argument.
``detunings``
    array ``(n_fields,)``, cyclic fixed detuning of each field.
``decay_scale``
    scalar multiplying every decay rate.
``omega0``
    array ``(n_fields, n_t)``, the input field samples on ``tlist`` as a
    *cyclic* Rabi frequency, the same unit as ``rabi_freq``. If given, the
    first slice is driven by their cubic spline instead of the analytic
    pulse (and ``pulse_args`` / ``rabi_freq`` are unused).

All parameters are cyclic (like the problem definition), and so is the
propagated field. It is returned in the layout and units of
``PropagationSolver.rabi_freqs_zt``: shape ``(n_fields, z_steps + 1, n_t)``,
complex, *cyclic* Rabi frequency, the same unit as ``rabi_freq`` and
``omega0``.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name            | Type   | Description                                                                                                                  |
|-----------------|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GRAD_CACHE_SIZE |        | how many compiled ``value_and_grad`` programs (one per loss function and mode) are kept; the least recently used is dropped. |

## Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

Counter-propagating fields are not supported. The result matches
``PropagationSolver`` for every ``z_steps_inner``; versions of clerq before
#328 stored Adams-Bashforth slices one inner step early when
``z_steps_inner > 1`` and will not match there.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                    | Default    |
|-------------|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| setup       | PropagationSetup | the problem, from ``setup_from_solver``.                                                                                                                                                       | _required_ |
| step        | str              | ``"ab"`` (Adams-Bashforth, default) or ``"euler"``.                                                                                                                                            | `'ab'`     |
| strategy    | str              | ``"s3"`` (default) recomputes a slice on the backward pass; ``"s2"`` stores every slice; ``"s4"`` additionally limits the solver's inner checkpoints to ``checkpoints``.                       | `'s3'`     |
| checkpoints | int \| None      | inner checkpoint count, required (a positive integer) for ``strategy="s4"`` and not allowed with the other strategies.                                                                         | `None`     |
| rtol        | float            | relative tolerance of the adaptive step-size control.                                                                                                                                          | `1e-08`    |
| atol        | float            | absolute tolerance of the adaptive step-size control.                                                                                                                                          | `1e-10`    |
| max_steps   | int              | the most steps one slice solve may take (the solve errors if it needs more); reverse mode sizes its default checkpoint count from it, so a smaller value lowers memory use for large problems. | `100000`   |
| n_steps     | int \| None      | fixed-step solver with this many steps per slice (useful for finite-difference reference gradients); must not be commensurate with the time grid.                                              | `None`     |
| solver      | Any              | a diffrax solver, default ``Tsit5``.                                                                                                                                                           | `None`     |

### clear_cache { #clerq.autodiff.AutodiffPropagation.clear_cache }

```python
autodiff.AutodiffPropagation.clear_cache()
```

Drop the compiled programs, releasing the loss functions (and the arrays
they capture) that ``value_and_grad`` keeps alive.

```python
autodiff.AutodiffPropagation.default_params()
```

The parameters of the problem this object was built from.

Every value is a float, whatever literal the problem definition used.

|--------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|

### value_and_grad { #clerq.autodiff.AutodiffPropagation.value_and_grad }

```python
autodiff.AutodiffPropagation.value_and_grad(
    loss,
    params=None,
    *,
    fixed=None,
    mode='reverse',
)
```

Value and gradient of ``loss(Omega_zt)`` with respect to ``params``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Default     |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| loss   | Callable     | scalar-valued function of the propagated field ``Omega_zt``, shape ``(n_fields, z_steps + 1, n_t)``, complex. Reuse the same function object between calls to reuse the compiled program: it is compiled once per function object, and only the last ``GRAD_CACHE_SIZE`` (8) are kept, so a new lambda on every call recompiles every time.                | _required_  |
| params | dict \| None | the parameters to differentiate (any subset of the keys; the gradient has the same structure). Default: every differentiable parameter of the problem, i.e. ``default_params()`` without the edge times (``on``, ``off``) of ``square`` pulses, which stay fixed because the field's derivative with respect to a discontinuity's location is not defined. | `None`      |
| fixed  | dict \| None | parameters held constant at the given values, with the same structure as ``params`` (for example the ``on``/``off`` of a square pulse, or a different target interaction strength). They are not differentiated.                                                                                                                                           | `None`      |
| mode   | str          | ``"reverse"`` (cost ~5x one propagation regardless of the number of parameters) or ``"forward"`` (cost grows with the number of parameters; useful as a cross-check or for very few parameters).                                                                                                                                                           | `'reverse'` |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type               | Description                                                            |
|--------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | tuple\[Any, dict\] | ``(value, grads)`` with ``grads`` of the same structure as ``params``. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                                                                                            |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | RuntimeError | if JAX is not in 64-bit mode.                                                                                          |
|        | ValueError   | for an unknown ``mode``, unknown keys, wrong shapes, or a request for the gradient of a ``square`` pulse's edge times. |
